SokoIow Podlaski New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sokołów Podlaski, Poland

Jewish settlement in Sokołów Podlaski developed from the 16th-17th century; population reached 70% (7,745) by 1910, settling at 4,430 by 1921, mostly murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery's land was purchased through a March 12, 1920 notarial deed; per the town's Memorial Book, it was 'established about 50 years before the extermination of the Jewish community.' The American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee funded pre-1939 fencing. Postwar destruction included gravel mining and illegal dumping; the District Court transferred cemetery responsibility to the State Treasury in 1959, and Poland formally closed it on December 6, 1963. A 1991 provincial intervention leveled remaining excavation pits and posted a warning sign against further gravel extraction.
